sources.entry: PrivyDrop - Simple and user-friendly, breakpoint-resumable peer-to-peer text, image, and file transfer tool based on WebRTC. (Source Code) MIT Docker/Nodejs

summary.one_liner: PrivyDrop is a browser-based, WebRTC peer-to-peer tool for sending text, images, files, and folders directly between devices without a server relaying the data.
summary.what_it_does: PrivyDrop transfers files, folders, and rich text directly between browsers over WebRTC, so content does not pass through a central server. A Node.js/Express backend with Socket.IO and Redis handles signaling, while the Next.js frontend provides the UI. Multiple receivers can join one room and download at the same time, and a link or QR code is used to invite them. When the save directory is set, Chrome can stream large files straight to disk, and interrupted transfers can resume from the point of interruption. The README notes that after an interruption, both sender and receiver pages must currently be refreshed to restart. Deployment is covered by a Docker script with several modes (LAN HTTP, LAN TLS, public IP, full domain with Let's Encrypt) and an optional TURN server.
use_cases: share files between my own devices in a browser
send large files without uploading to a cloud service
share a folder or several files with multiple people at once
send formatted text or clipboard content to another device
self-host a private LAN file transfer page
transfer files over a LAN with optional TURN for NAT traversal
how_to_run: git clone <repo> && cd PrivyDrop && sudo apt-get install -y redis-server
cd backend && npm install && cp .env_development_example .env.development && npm run dev
cd frontend && pnpm install && cp .env_development_example .env.development && pnpm dev
Open the frontend address in your browser and start sharing
notable: Peer-to-peer transfer over WebRTC with no server-side data relay
Chrome direct-to-disk streaming for files of any size when a save directory is set
Multiple receivers can download from one room, and new receivers can join mid-transfer
One-command Docker deployment with LAN, public IP, and domain modes, including optional TURN and Let's Encrypt
In-app navigation keeps ongoing transfers alive via a singleton Zustand store and webrtcService
caveats: Resume needs a save directory set, and after an interruption both sender and receiver pages must be refreshed to restart
LAN TLS uses a self-signed CA that must be imported into each browser or system trust store
Requires Redis for the backend and Node.js v18+ for local development
keywords: send files to phone from browser
